about: BayCounty.me Accountability console: public projects from first budget to close-out, with timeline events, flags from published rules, records still missing, and each agency's reply. A flag is a question for the agency, not a finding of wrongdoing.

rules.title: Cost grew more than 10%
rules.when: The latest firm figure (final cost, current contract total or current project estimate) is more than 10% above the first firm figure (the award or first budget). Over 25% is marked high.
rules.means: The project costs noticeably more than the public was first told. Bay County and Panama City require board approval once change orders pass 10%.
rules.not: It does not mean money was wasted. Scope added on purpose, design and land costs, and price changes all raise totals. The flag asks the agency to explain the difference.

rules.title: Running late
rules.when: A source reports the project finished more than 90 days after its schedule, or a sales tax project is not complete after the last year it was programmed for. Over a year is marked high.
rules.means: The public waited longer than planned, which often costs money too.
rules.not: Delays are often caused by utilities, permits, storms or grant timing outside the agency's control.

rules.title: Figures don't agree
rules.when: Two or more public documents give different amounts for the same project and period.
rules.means: Residents cannot tell from the public record what the project costs or what was spent.
rules.not: The documents may count different things (one phase, the CRA share, the whole project). The agency can settle it with one breakdown.

rules.title: Who was paid isn't public yet
rules.when: Money was spent or committed, but no record we have names the contractor or seller, or states the price.
rules.means: The public cannot check who received the money or for how much.
rules.not: The information usually exists in the agency's files; it just wasn't in the report we read. A records request will usually get it.

rules.title: Local share unclear
rules.when: The project mixes CRA or city money with state or federal grants, and no record says how much is local tax money.
rules.means: The totals shown overstate what local taxpayers paid, by an unknown amount.
rules.not: Grants are good for local taxpayers. The flag is only about knowing the split.

rules.title: Budgeted, but spending not shown
rules.when: A budget was set, but actual spending is under half of it for a year that has ended, or no record of actual spending was found.
rules.means: The money may be sitting unspent, may have been moved, or the work stalled.
rules.not: Unspent budgets often roll over to the next year, and a delayed project may still be on track overall.

rules.title: Approval not found in the minutes
rules.when: A change order appeared on an agenda, but the meeting minutes we read do not record a vote approving it.
rules.means: We could not confirm the board approved the added cost.
rules.not: It may have been approved on a consent agenda, in minutes we have not read, or by staff within their authority.

rules.title: More than one incentive, same place
rules.when: One address or company receives more than one grant or rebate from the same agency.
rules.means: The total public support is easy to miss when each award is reported on its own.
rules.not: Programs usually allow this. The flag adds it up; it does not say it was wrong.

rules.title: Dropped from the schedule
rules.when: A project was struck from the sales tax project schedule.
rules.means: Money promised to voters for this project went elsewhere or is on hold.
rules.not: Schedules are amended when costs, grants or priorities change; the replacement project may be listed.
